articles.title: MindsEye Developers Say They've Been Laid Off Amid Questions Over Build a Rocket Boy's Future
articles.summary: Multiple developers of the disastrous MindsEye have said they’ve been laid off, casting doubt over the future of its controversial developer, Build A Rocket Boy.
articles.body:
Multiple developers of the disastrous MindsEye have said they’ve been laid off, casting doubt over the future of its controversial developer, Build A Rocket Boy.

Story-driven action adventure game MindsEye was initially designed to be a part of Everywhere, the ‘Roblox for adults’ creation platform led by former Grand Theft Auto design chief Leslie Benzies. BARB eventually switched to focus on MindsEye, with the company ballooning in size to over 500 staff at peak.

But MindsEye flopped hard when it came out in June 2025, with players calling it "broken," "buggy," and "the worst game of 2025." Soon after, BARB said it was “heartbroken” over the issues players had faced with the game , and promised to release a series of patches to fix the significant performance problems, glitches, and AI behavior bugs. Benzies told staff that the studio would bounce back and relaunch MindsEye, blaming its struggles on internal and external "saboteurs," among other things. CEO Mark Gerhard said the studio had been investigating what he called “criminal activity” that took place around the launch of the game.

In July last year, IGN reported that the Scottish studio had issued at-risk of redundancy emails to its then around 300-strong UK workforce. Subsequent rounds of layoffs followed, and this summer, fired staff protested outside the studio over an “all-expenses-paid playtest day.”

BARB attempted to relaunch MindsEye with what was called the “Blacklisted” update, but it failed to move the needle. Subsequent updates and a last-ditch 50% off Steam sale have similarly fallen on deaf ears. While console player numbers are unavailable, MindsEye had a 24-hour peak Steam concurrent player count of just 16.

The extent of the layoffs is unclear at this stage, with one source familiar with the studio telling IGN that the company may not be dissolved even if all staff are let go. Either way, there are now serious questions over the future of the studio and MindsEye itself. IGN has asked BARB for comment.

Benzies was a crucial member of the Grand Theft Auto development team at Rockstar, and is considered one of the key architects of its enormous success. He left in 2016 amid a legal row over unpaid royalties that was eventually settled out of court. With the GTA link in place, BARB attracted more than £233 million ($313 million) of investment by 2024. Hitman developer IO Interactive snapped up publishing rights.

BARB's latest financial statements, made up to September 30, 2025, reveal it had generated revenue of £4.6 million ($6.1 million), but had total operating costs of £52.1 million ($70 million). It declared a net loss of £36.2 million ($48.6 million) for the period.

In May, Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, issued what sounded like a nod to BARB’s struggles . "Making hits seems to get harder and harder and harder as entertainment industries mature," Zelnick said, speaking at the TD Cowen 54th Annual Technology, Media & Telecom Conference.

"The folks at Rockstar seem to be able to make these massive hits, and lots of other people have tried. Lots and lots, including former Rockstar employees. And so far, they haven't been able to do it."

articles.title: Baby Born in Movie Theater During Harry Potter Now Has 'Cineworld' Listed as Place of Birth
articles.summary: A baby girl now has "Cineworld" listed as her official place of birth, after popping out during a recent screening of Harry Potter.
articles.body:
A baby girl now has "Cineworld" listed as her official place of birth, after popping out during a recent Harry Potter screening.

Elsie Lamb was born around 45 minutes into Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (that's Sorcerer's Stone if you're in the U.S.). And now, officially, her birthplace has been recorded as the Cineworld movie theater in Broughton, North Wales.

BBC News reports that Potter-mad mom Molly Connah, 32, was overdue to give birth and had attended an appointment just hours earlier for a sweep — a process meant to encourage the start of labor. What happened next, then, could probably have been predicted — even if it still might have seemed like magic.

Harry Potter HBO TV Series Cast and Characters: Who's Confirmed for the Reboot?

"I can remember the scene I was watching when I walked out," Connah said. "It was when Hagrid and Harry are buying his stuff to go to Hogwarts. I thought, 'something doesn't feel right'.

"It was getting more and more intense, and I didn't want anything to go wrong," she continued. "At that point I think my body just went into shock and it was pure adrenalin."

Thankfully, Connah was assisted by her mom, as well as staff at the Cineworld and nearby Starbucks, who provided towels and sheets.

"I said to my mum, 'I feel like I need to push,'" Connah recalled. "She said, 'you can't'. I said, 'I can't, I need to. I've got to'. Two pushes and my daughter was out."

Within minutes, an emergency medic and also Elsie Lamb's father had both made it to the scene, and the family was then transferred to hospital before the film's credits rolled. All are now doing well, it's reported, and have visited the Cineworld again to thank staff for their help.

Cineworld, meanwhile, have given the family four free tickets to a future showing, as they missed the end of the movie.

Harry Potter recently returned to theaters in celebration of the first film's 25th anniversary , and so Warner Bros. could wring out one last bit of nostalgia for its movies before the franchise is rebooted via HBO's Harry Potter TV series that debuts this Christmas.

articles.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Surpasses Star Wars: The Force Awakens to Become North America's Highest-Grossing Movie of All Time
articles.summary: Spider-Man: Brand New Day has overtaken Star Wars: The Force Awakens to become the highest-grossing movie of all time in North America.
articles.body:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day has overtaken Star Wars: The Force Awakens to become the highest-grossing movie of all time in North America.

Domestic box office for the Tom Holland sequel is now up to $936.773 million, according to Variety . That puts it just ahead of 2015’s The Force Awakens, which is sitting on $936 million at the North American box office.

Of course, The Force Awakens came out 11 years ago, so there’s inflation to consider here. But Sony and Marvel owner Disney won’t care; Spider-Man: Brand New Day has been an astonishing success, so much so that even movie executives were taken by surprise.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day - Our Biggest Burning Questions

If you’re one of the few who hasn’t seen Brand New Day yet, it picks up years after the events of 2021’s No Way Home, and shows Peter Parker struggling to cope with the absence of his friends and loved ones following Doctor Strange’s memory wipe spell. A decent chunk of the first act of the movie is spent showing Parker’s inner turmoil and, yes, his extreme loneliness, which is fueled by the end of his relationship with Zendaya’s MJ.

This, Rothman insisted, is the key to Brand New Day’s appeal. Brand New Day is “not so much a superhero film, but a super-person film,” he said. “The reason that movie has resonated all around the world is because it’s about a lonely guy… It’s like yeah, it’s about friendship. It’s very human. It’s very emotional. It’s got plenty of whiz-bang, but that’s not what the secret is. The secret is it’s a relatable story that almost everybody has related to.”

The big box office question now is will Brand New Day go on to hit the billion dollar mark at the domestic box office? As Variety notes, after 47 days in theaters, perhaps it will need a re-release or two to get there.

Brand New Day’s global total is now $2.4 billion, which makes it the third-highest grossing movie of all time behind only Avatar and Avengers: Endgame. Neither movie is in trouble of being overtaken by Brand New Day (Endgame is on $2.7 billion, Avatar, which came out in 2009, is on $2.9 billion).

Last week, it was reported that the inevitable Spider-Man sequel already has its director , with Deadline saying Destin Daniel Cretton will return for Marvel and Sony's fifth Tom Holland-starring Spider-Man movie. Given how well Cretton’s Brand New Day has done, that’s not a huge surprise.

Will this December’s Avengers: Doomsday , which has yet to confirm the appearance of a Spider-Man from this or any other universe, outperform Brand New Day?

articles.title: Resident Evil Director Zach Cregger Reveals His Pick to Play Lady Dimitrescu
articles.summary: Resident Evil director Zach Cregger has revealed which actress he would cast as a live-action Lady Dimitrescu — and we think he's made the perfect choice.
articles.body:
Resident Evil director Zach Cregger has revealed which actress he would cast as a live-action Lady Dimitrescu — and we think he's made the perfect choice.

To be clear, the iconic Lady D from 2021's Resident Evil Village does not appear in Cregger's upcoming Resident Evil movie, as it tells an original story. So, don't expect to see her or any other fan favorites up on the big screen. That said, Cregger is a self-confessed Resident Evil aficionado, and seems to clearly know who he'd cast if given the chance.

"Christina Hendricks," Cregger said, when asked his pick for Lady D while in conversation with Pedestrian.TV . "That feels about right to me. What do you think?" Well, speaking personally, that seems like a solid call.

Resident Evil Village: The Mercenaries Additional Orders Screenshots

The vampire-like Lady Dimitrscu stole the hearts of many Resident Evil fans back when Village launched, with many players attracted to her giant stature and femme fatale design. Countless pieces of fan art followed, some more erotic than others, and Capcom leant into her popularity by providing life-size cardboard cutouts of the character in video game stores.

Even though Lady D hasn't returned to the series (so far), she remains a firm favorite — and notably her costume could be unlocked in this year's Resident Evil Requiem , if you stumped up for the game's Deluxe Edition.

Could we see the character appear in a future Resident Evil film? While Cregger has taken flak from some fans for deciding to make an original take on the franchise, early buzz for the movie has been positive, and the box office projections look strong. Indeed, Cregger has already said he has ideas for potential sequels. Here's hoping Christina Hendricks is free.

articles.title: Call of Duty Developer Treyarch 'Ready to Make Something New' as It Waves Goodbye to 2 Years of Black Ops
articles.summary: Call of Duty developer Treyarch has said it’s “ready to make something new” as it waves goodbye to two years of Black Ops games.
articles.body:
Call of Duty developer Treyarch has said it’s “ready to make something new” as it waves goodbye to two years of Black Ops games.

Treyarch led development on two Black Ops games back-to-back: 2024’s Black Ops 6 and 2025’s Black Ops 7. With Season 6 hitting Black Ops 7 on September 17, the developer has signalled it’s moving on to its next Call of Duty game.

“This is a bittersweet goodbye, but I think over the last two years, we've learned a lot,” design director Kevin Drew said in a new dev talk video . “We've tried a lot of things in our current era. But we're ready to make something new and something that nobody's ever experienced before. In the meantime though, I will see you all playing in Season 6 on September 17th.”

What this means, exactly, is unclear. Could Treyarch be talking about making a new Call of Duty game not in the Black Ops subbrand? Is Treyarch’s next Call of Duty not Black Ops 8? That would be something of a surprise, given Black Ops’ popularity and brand power despite Black Ops 7’s high-profile commercial struggles . Perhaps Treyarch is talking about doing something brand new within the Black Ops universe. My feeling though, is that this is indeed a hint that Black Ops may be given some time to rest, and that Treyarch has something different up its sleeve.

Yale Miller, co-studio head, added: “It’s been amazing to look back at the last couple of years, setting new benchmarks with Black Ops 6, delivering the biggest Black Ops game ever with Black Ops 7, taking huge swings with Omnimovement, Endgame, all kinds of innovation. We are extremely proud and extremely excited for what we were able to deliver.

“So, it's been amazing to actually also have a dialogue with all of you through regular comms, also through these dev talks, and we've been along with you every step of the way while we're delivering new innovative content. You guys have been grinding out camos, unlocking new things, the progression systems, the feedback. A huge thank you to our partner Raven and all the other studios that helped us here at Treyarch bring all of you all those maps, all that content, all those zombies experiences. It's been amazing.

“Really excited as well for everything Infinity Ward has been working on. They are clearly setting new bars. There's so much more of that game for all of you to see. We've had the privilege of taking part in a ton of playtests as well. We'll see you all online in Season 6 and in MW4. Thank you so much. It has been a privilege.”

Infinity Ward’s Modern Warfare 4 comes out later this year, but Activision has yet to say what will follow. It has an army of studios working on Call of Duty, which may need a shot in the arm from, say, Sledgehammer or Warzone developer Raven in the coming years. The question for parent company Microsoft and new Xbox boss Asha Sharma will be, how does Call of Duty once again hit the heights of yesteryear?

articles.title: Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil Movie Amplifies Classic Gameplay Moments Into Horror Movie Beats Without Having to Delve Into Fan Service
articles.summary: Review: With a laser focus on putting its hero through the worst night of his life, Resident Evil is a simple and exciting survival horror story that benefits greatly from director Zach Cregger’s sensibilities.
articles.body:
Resident Evil is in theaters on September 18.

Whatever your idea of what a good Resident Evil movie should be, I have to recommend to the skeptical to put that to one side and lock in for what Zach Cregger delivers with this new adaptation of the Capcom games. With a clear appreciation for odds stacked against the protagonist and all manner of freaky foes to stand against them, Cregger ably adapts the spirit, if not the letter, of the Resident Evil games into a jet-fueled horror experience that has room for lots of tension, some great laughs, and a strong central performance from Austin Abrams.

What’s clear about Resident Evil from the first frame is that it’s got some serious pep in its step. At 95 minutes, Resident Evil is here for a good time, not a long time, and it hits the ground running as Bryan (Austin Abrams), a medical courier, accepts a last-minute assignment to bring a high-priority delivery through the mountains to Raccoon City General Hospital. We encounter our first zombie less than 10 minutes past that point, and from there, Cregger doesn’t ever let too long go by without putting Bryan through some funhouse maze of grotesquery he’s ill-equipped to contend with, and to frequently hilarious effect.

Yes, Resident Evil is often very funny, but never in a way that feels at the franchise’s expense. Cregger is broadly successful in judging how and when to lean into the campy nature of Resident Evil’s pedigree for comedic effect, or to what degree Bryan’s ineptitude should detour the action into a less predictable direction. Cregger is adept at building tension in a way that makes it impossible to get a read on if that tension will pay off in a laugh or a scare, and that unpredictable energy permeates Resident Evil. This dark comedic streak is a signature of Cregger’s at this point, and it’s a surprising and effective counterbalance to the world-shaking ramifications of the Raccoon City incident currently underway. Ironically, it’s only the handful of Resident Evil’s meta jokes about its video game heritage that ring a little hollow and dated; other than that, Cregger is largely very successful at understanding how to adapt a video game into a movie in a way that serves both mediums well, even when that means subverting expectations.

And as far as heroes go, Austin Abrams’ Bryan is definitely one for subverting expectations. Far from the Leon Kennedy or Chris Redfield action-hero mold, Bryan is an everyman just trying to make a bit of extra cash and navigate some high-stakes relationship issues with his offscreen girlfriend Michelle. After his scene-stealing turn in Weapons , Abrams easily shoulders his promotion to leading man here in a performance that’s a lot more skillful than the simplicity of the character first suggests. Abrams spends long stretches of Resident Evil as the only (human) actor onscreen, and Cregger pushes him into numerous scenarios where Bryan has to narrate his way through what he’s doing, often while also delivering on a comedic beat at the same time. The actor takes the frenetic energy of his Weapons character (he was the drug addict burglar in that movie) and focuses it down into something just as nervy, but a lot more grounded and relatable.

Yes, Bryan reacts like a normal human probably should when faced with tentacle monsters exploding out of places they shouldn’t, and Abrams and Cregger both really seem to delight in the character’s frequent overwhelm. It’s played for laughs most of the time, but that tendency towards being overwhelmed also forms the backbone of what simple character arc there is for Bryan to reckon with in the aftermath of his conversations with Michelle. Resident Evil makes no secret about what Bryan is struggling to wrap his head around, even as everyone around him devolves into snarling monsters, and though the movie doesn’t go very far out of its way to land any of that with any real weight, Bryan’s anxieties are serviceable enough to give structure and add some dimension to a few of the later encounters he has to survive.

It’s a good thing that Abrams is as watchable as he is, because no member of Resident Evil’s supporting cast gets much more to do than drop in for a scene or two’s worth of exposition. No one’s bad acting-wise, there’s just very little room for anyone in the supporting cast to be really good. Paul Walter Hauser’s Umbrella Corporation functionary has just enough time in the spotlight to illustrate how terrible the Umbrella Corporation is, but characters like these are the trees on the side of the road that Resident Evil is racing by as it moves from beat to beat. As long as you’re having a good time with Abrams behind the wheel, this won’t matter at all, but if you’re on the fence, you may find yourself wishing you’d gotten some more time with some of Raccoon City’s citizenry.

Of course, the real stars here are the poor, unfortunate souls afflicted by the t-Virus, which has a habit of rapidly mutating any human tissue it comes into contact with. There are some zombies here and there, but they’re as disposable to the experience of watching Resident Evil as they are to playing any Resident Evil game. It’s the more creative, nightmarish mutants which have evolved past “vanilla zombie” that really keep Resident Evil moving. By the time Cregger has trotted out just the film’s second infected creature, it’s clear that nothing breathing can be trusted not to erupt in a mess of whipping appendages and eyeballs, and more movies could use that kind of uncertainty as a ticking time bomb to take advantage of.

These creatures, which feel right at home with Resident Evil’s Lovecraftian design language, are all lovingly rendered by Cregger and his team, who luxuriate in their oozing, thrashing, slithering glory. Abrams’ big, shrieking reactions to these horrors feels more and more appropriate as the movie goes because they get increasingly disturbing (and blissfully, most of the good stuff has been held back from the marketing). Bryan’s journey to the heart of Raccoon City really becomes an excuse to tour as much of this genetic hellscape as possible, which means that the cycle of “new location, new gross monster to sidestep” may get tiresome, but the creativity of how Cregger introduces and then heightens these things often feels like it outpaces the rinse and repeat nature of how we discover them as we go.

With an obvious tendency towards celebrating the feel of the games and not the specifics of the plot, Resident Evil consistently succeeds in amplifying classic gameplay moments from the franchise into horror movie beats in a way that goes far beyond simple fan service and “I understood that reference” references. Searching for ammo, spotting an oncoming enemy, reloading on a time crunch as they close distance, getting a perfectly timed shot off, being lured into the dark by something you may not be equipped to deal with… Cregger’s Resident Evil is littered with touches like these that are actually used to ratchet up moment-to-moment dread and not just to pay lip service to gamers.

That carries through into Dariusz Wolski’s cinematography, which emphasizes Bryan’s perspective throughout and frequently emulates the third-person approach of the games in a way that heightens the terror of what we may find around the next corner. Wolski also plays with different light sources really well throughout Resident Evil, especially in an early scene where both the exterior and interior lights of a car are used to moody and tense effect as things go wrong on a snow-driven road. Co-composers Ryan and Hays Holladay also support Cregger’s efforts with a discordant, playful score that finds a good balance between boldly accentuating big moments and keeping tension simmering on the burner as Bryan stumbles his way through dark, new spaces.

articles.title: Pirate Who Cracked Denuvo Games Like Resident Evil Requiem Plans to Keep Doing So Despite Being Sued
articles.summary: A pirate known for cracking games that utilize the DRM software Denuvo is being hit with a lawsuit... but that isn't stopping them from continuing on.
articles.body:
A pirate known for cracking games that utilize the DRM software Denuvo is being hit with a lawsuit... but that isn't stopping them from continuing on.

For years, PC games have attempted to shield themselves from piracy with a DRM software known as Denuvo. The software is meant to be difficult to crack, with the hope that it will protect the game from becoming available for free on piracy sites around the time of launch. It does its job to a degree, as it took about a month and a half for Resident Evil Requiem to be cracked ... and it was achieved by a pirate known as voices38.

As spotted by GamesRadar , the pirate is now being sued by Denuvo, so long as the company can actually identify who they are. The company is working to unmask this anonymous pirate and there's likely hope that even if they aren't successful, the pressure of an investigation will maybe spook voices38 into disappearing. That's not the case, though. voices38 took to Reddit to issue a statement, telling fellow pirates that "all is fine" and "everything will continue as normal."

It's an interesting story, and one that only feels all the more relevant with the recent GTA 6 leaks , when a leaker obtained access to the build of the highly anticipated game and taunted Rockstar Games with various messages. Once the game was properly revealed, the leaker vanished, and as of a month later, there has been no word as to whether or not they've been caught. Whether they'll return to cause more chaos remains to be seen, but it is pretty evident that online hackers and lawbreakers are getting good at evading detection.

Whether voices38 can continue to crack these games and get away with it is up in the air, but they certainly think they can.

articles.title: Quentin Tarantino’s New Novel The Adventures of Cliff Booth Is Up for Preorder
articles.summary: Quentin Tarantino has a new novel coming out in December called The Adventures of Cliff Booth. It's a novelization of the upcoming Brad Pitt movie, and it's available to preorder now.
articles.body:
Here’s one for film buffs who also enjoy curling up with a good book: Quentin Tarantino has a new novel coming out soon. It’s called The Adventures of Cliff Booth, and it’s a novelization of the upcoming movie The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , which is a stand-alone sequel to Once Upon a Time in Hollywood. The book is up for preorder on Amazon for $32, with a release date of December 8.

The Adventures of Cliff Booth: A Novel (Hardcover)

According to the blurb, the book follows the Brad Pitt character Cliff Booth, a “war hero, stuntman, bartender, cinema projectionist,” as he navigates 1977 Hollywood, performing “clandestine services” for his friends. Since Once Upon a Time in Hollywood toook place in 1969, that means this is set eight years after the exciting events of that movie.

That’s about all we know so far about the book – or the movie for that matter (you can watch the all-vibes trailer here ). It looks like Netflix re-named the movie just two weeks ago from “The Adventures of Cliff Booth” to “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth,” so we shall see if the same title change comes to the book in the future. In the meantime, you can lock in your preorder now and it’ll ship on December 8, when it’s released.

This isn’t the first time Tarantino has penned a novel. He also wrote a novelization for Once Upon a Time in Hollywood that’s currently on sale at Amazon for $6 . Tarantino isn’t just writing novels for goofs, either. The New York Times gave that book a positive review , calling it a “pulpy page-turner.” In 2022, Tarantino also published a nonfiction book called Cinema Speculation .

The movie version of The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth hits IMAX theaters on November 25 for an exclusive two-week window, followed by its release on Netflix on December 23. For Tarantino fans, it will be a merry Christmas indeed.

articles.title: El Barça no puede fichar a Julián Álvarez... ni en EA Sports FC 27
articles.standfirst: Algunos streamers ya pueden jugar al videojuego, y el directo de RobertPG ha dejado un momentazo
articles.summary: Algunos streamers ya pueden jugar al videojuego, y el directo de RobertPG ha dejado un momentazo
articles.body: El FC Barcelona sigue teniendo problemas para fichar a Julián Álvarez. El delantero argentino ya fue uno de los grandes protagonistas del mercado de fichajes de este verano, cuando el Atlético de Madrid dejó muy claro que no estaba dispuesto a negociar su salida. Una situación que parece haberse trasladado también al mundo de los videojuegos, concretamente a EA Sports FC 27. Muchos creadores de contenido ya están pudiendo disfrutar de las primeras horas con el nuevo título de fútbol de Electronic Arts. Uno de ellos es RobertPG, que decidió aprovechar la oportunidad para ponerse al frente del conjunto blaugrana en el Modo Carrera e intentar redimirse tras lo sucedido este verano con el delantero argentino. La idea era sencilla: si el Barça no había conseguido fichar a Julián Álvarez en la vida real, quizás sí podría hacerlo dentro del videojuego. Sin embargo, lo que se encontró el creador de contenido fue una situación que seguro que no esperaba. El Atlético de Madrid ni tan siquiera quiso sentarse a negociar por su delantero. Una negativa que dejó al jugador fuera del alcance del conjunto catalán y que provocó una reacción de sorpresa por parte de RobertPG. Porque una cosa es que el Atlético no quiera vender a Julián Álvarez en la realidad, pero otra muy distinta es que tampoco permita negociar por él en el Modo Carrera. Y ojo, que esto es precisamente lo que hace que la situación tenga todavía más gracia. El videojuego parece haber decidido ponerse serio con el mercado de fichajes y trasladar al terreno virtual uno de los grandes culebrones del fútbol español. Lo que está claro es que, si el Modo Carrera sigue evolucionando por este camino, al final será más difícil fichar a los jugadores dentro del propio videojuego que en la vida real. Y eso ya es mucho decir. Así que ya sabes, esto es EA Sports FC 27, donde los dramas del mercado de fichajes no terminan cuando se apaga la televisión. También llegan al mundo de los videojuegos.

articles.title: Marvel's Wolverine Players Are Testing Its Motorcycle Sequence to See if Logan Can Die if You Don't Touch the Controller
articles.summary: Marvel’s Wolverine has kicked off no end of debates on social media, with the latest of these centering around a chase sequence that sees Logan weaving through traffic on a motorcycle.
articles.body:
Marvel’s Wolverine has kicked off no end of debates on social media, with the latest of these centering around a chase sequence that sees Logan weaving through traffic on a motorcycle.

Insomniac’s new superhero game is the latest hot-button topic in the gaming community. Well before it even released, players were calling out early gameplay footage shown off by the media, taking umbrage with a Sentinel boss fight (it was too formulaic), its voice acting (who hired these anime voice actors for my grisly X-Men game?) and Logan following a scent trail to track down enemies (too hand-holdy).

Now that it’s finally out in the wild, players have had a swath of mixed opinions on the title; some are absolutely loving it and finding it a decent challenge, while others are disappointed by its combat, perceived lack of difficulty, and impossible-to-fail QTEs.

This last complaint has reared its head specifically around a sequence where players are meant to chase down enemies on a motorcycle, dodging and weaving through traffic on a winding highway in the mountains. Logan is desperately trying to rescue a group of captured mutants who’ve been shoved onto a truck, and the situation is dire — but some players have discovered that he’ll successfully catch up to the bad guys regardless of whether or not you actually pilot him in the right direction.

One of the most viral examples of this came from an X user named Clint Beastwood, who claimed to have put down his controller to see what would happen to Logan if he didn’t interfere. The result was Logan bouncing off of guard rails like a high-stakes game of pinball, somehow making his way through the sequence without dying.

However, it is possible for him to die after getting hit by on coming vehicles, though he’s paradoxically more likely to meet an untimely end if players actually take hold of the controller and try to help him avoid ending up like a bug on someone’s windshield.

He CAN die. You do not need to control the bike. pic.twitter.com/6mPKHnxNne — Clint Beastwood (@woodbeastclint) September 15, 2026

He CAN die. You do not need to control the bike. pic.twitter.com/6mPKHnxNne

The resulting conversation has been a heated one; players are at odds with each other, with some finding this a comparatively small issue in a sequence meant to get players from point A to point B, while others, like YouTuber ChicoFilo, are calling the lack of player agency “just ridiculous.”

“This here is a total disgrace,” Brazilian influencer Eloohzinha said. “It's [a] QTE that you don't even need to press, it's a bike that you don't need to ride.”

Isso aqui é esculacho total. É QTE que você nao precisa apertar, é moto que voce nao precisa pilotar. É pérola atras de perola. Realmente, o prego no caixão foi esse wolverine. Ultimo jogo bom do estudio foi Ratchet And Clank e ja era. pic.twitter.com/hRUFzxmNDe — Eloohzinha (@__Mc_Gonagall__) September 14, 2026

Isso aqui é esculacho total. É QTE que você nao precisa apertar, é moto que voce nao precisa pilotar. É pérola atras de perola. Realmente, o prego no caixão foi esse wolverine. Ultimo jogo bom do estudio foi Ratchet And Clank e ja era. pic.twitter.com/hRUFzxmNDe

Decided to play Wolverine on the HARDEST difficulty and honestly it's been fun but this is just ridiculous 😭 #Wolverine #Playstation pic.twitter.com/fnoqSKazV6 — ChicoFilo (@ChicoFiloYT) September 16, 2026

Decided to play Wolverine on the HARDEST difficulty and honestly it's been fun but this is just ridiculous 😭 #Wolverine #Playstation pic.twitter.com/fnoqSKazV6

“If Wolverine gets hit while on the bike, he can die. So you do need to control the bike. It’s posts like this that hurt real conversations around games,” popular YouTuber Mightykeef argued. “...if you can die, then it’s not autopilot. You need to control the bike, or else you can die and start over again. This type of on-rails segment happens in hundreds of action games.”

“Keyword being ‘if,’ when ‘if’ shouldn’t exist,” another user hit back. “There’s plenty of videos already out there showing players getting through the entire sequence without dying, regardless of difficulty.”

Keyword being “ IF “ when “ IF “ shouldn’t exist. There’s plenty of videos already out there showing players getting through the entire sequence without dying. Regardless of difficulty. — 𝓛𝓪𝓽𝓲𝓷𝓛𝓮𝓰𝓪𝓬𝔂 (@LatinLegacy) September 15, 2026

Keyword being “ IF “ when “ IF “ shouldn’t exist. There’s plenty of videos already out there showing players getting through the entire sequence without dying. Regardless of difficulty.

For now, players will just have to pick up the game themselves to form their own opinions on it. We at IGN gave it a six out of 10 , saying its “good character work props up flashy combat that wears thin over time.” (Personally, I’m enjoying the game so far, and haven’t been annoyed by scent trails or QTEs just yet. I also liked the Omega Red boss fight, which seems to have been tripping up quite a few players onine.)

articles.title: Resident Evil Creator Shinji Mikami to Be Inducted Into D.I.C.E. Hall of Fame
articles.summary: Resident Evil creator Shinji Mikami will officially be honored with the Hall of Fame Award at the 30th Annual D.I.C.E. Awards ceremony on February 18, 2027.
articles.body:
Resident Evil creator Shinji Mikami will officially be honored with the Hall of Fame Award at the 30th Annual D.I.C.E. Awards ceremony on February 18, 2027.

The Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences (AIAS) announced the news today and shared that Grasshopper Manufacture's Goichi Suda (SUDA51) will present the award to his "close friend and creative collaborator."

“It was from Mikami-san that I learned how to approach game development, both as a director and as a designer. Of all the many Padawans Mikami-san has mentored, I’m truly honored that I was chosen to be his presenter for this induction into a kind of video game hall of fame,” said Suda. “As one such Padawan, please allow me to celebrate my Obi-Wan Kenobi, Shinji Mikami, through this honorable award. I’m sure Mikami-san’s innumerable fans and industry comrades are just as delighted as I am to see him receive such an amazing award.”

Mikami's career has spanned over 30 years and his catalog of games is nearly unmatched, including Resident Evil, Devil May Cry, Dino Crisis, The Evil Within, Hi-Fi Rush, Vanquish, Ghostwire: Tokyo, and many more.

He is currently the Creative Director and CEO of Unbound Inc., which was purchased by Stellar Blade developer Shift Up earlier this year and is currently working on an unannounced video game.

“Shinji Mikami is a monumental and influential figure for both fans and developers alike,” said Meggan Scavio, president of the AIAS. “He has continually demonstrated his originality and creative vision that resonates and inspires the action game genre. We are honored to be able to celebrate Mikami-san’s achievements and induct him into our Hall of Fame during our 30th anniversary of the D.I.C.E. Awards.”

Mikami will join such past AIAS Hall of Fame recipients as Evan Wells (2026), Ted Price (2025), Koji Kondo (2024), Tim Schafer (2022), Ed Boon (2021), Connie Booth (2020), Bonnie Ross (2019), and Todd Howard (2017).

For more, check out Mikami's thoughts on what makes a good remake and how it's up to developers to make games people want to play, not just stream.

articles.summary: The entire run of Star Trek: The Next Generation is on sale in digital HD format right now for $49 at Amazon.
articles.body:
Here’s an excellent deal for classic sci-fi enthusiasts. Right now, you can buy the entire series of Star Trek: The Next Generation (all 178 episodes) in HD digital for just $49.99 at Amazon . That’s a great deal, as it usually goes for way more than that.

Star Trek: The Next Generation - Complete Series for $49.99

Star Trek: The Next Generation - Complete Series

Star Trek TNG (as it’s known to super cool insiders like me) kicked off in 1987 and ran for seven seasons, ending in 1994. Back in those days, seasons were 26 episodes long, give or take – not the namby-pamby 8-episode orders many shows get today. That's a lot of content. If you watch one episode per day, it'll take you nearly six months to watch it all.

TNG has arguably the best captain of them all, Captain Jean-Luc Picard, played by the inimitable Patrick Stewart. The rest of the cast is stacked too, with Jonathan Frakes as Riker, Picard’s number one, along with Michael Dorn as Worf, Brent Spiner as Data, Gates McFaden as Dr. Crusher, and Marina Sirtis as Troi, to name a few.

General consensus among fans is that TNG took a couple of years to find its footing, and there’s some truth to that. But I still love the first two seasons, even if they’re not as thrilling as the later ones. It took the makers of the show some time to get a feel for the characters and eventually craft longer narrative arcs, but the whole series is worth watching (or re-watching).

I bought a digital copy of this series a few years ago for $100 and it has been worth every penny. This is one of my comfort shows, so I watch an episode whenever I need a pick-me-up. It’s great to have on hand, whether or not I’m currently subscribed to Paramount+ , the streaming service where all of Star Trek resides. (If you do want to stream them instead, you can get a pretty great deal on Paramount+ at the moment.)

It’s unclear how long this deal will last, so I’d grab it sooner rather than later if you’re interested. Make it so.

articles.title: Studio Behind Hyper Light Drifter In Peril After Publisher Withdraws Funding for Unannounced Project
articles.summary: Heart Machine, the development studio behind titles like Hyper Light Drifter and Possessors, is in dire straits after a publisher withdrew their funding for an unannounced project.
articles.body:
Heart Machine, the development studio behind titles like Hyper Light Drifter and Possessors, is in dire straits after a publisher withdrew their funding for an unannounced project.

The news was shared to LinkedIn by Heart Machine’s founder, Alx Preston, on September 16, 2026. Preston explained that the publisher funding this unannounced title “decided to no longer move forward with it,” and without this income, the studio was forced to lay off “nearly everyone.”

“It's devastating,” Preston wrote, going on to confirm that all people involved would be given “as much support as possible, including assisting with placement.”

Currently, Preston isn’t certain whether or not Heart Machine will survive this devastating financial blow, but says that its existing team will “keep pushing to build a path.”

“Thank you so so much to all of the incredible people who contributed their efforts and talents to making amazing things at the studio. Thank you to our amazing community and fans,” he said.

Heart Machine’s most recent offering, a search-action game titled Possessors , released in November 2025. It received mostly positive reviews from fans, with IGN’s Matt Kim calling it a “fast-paced action-adventure” with “rapid-fast” combat that lets players “wield a computer mouse like a whip.”

Its most famous title, Hyper Light Drifter , is a heavily-stylized 2D action game that has become a cult classic among fans over the last decade, with IGN praising it as a “gorgeous, fast, fluid trek in a neon apocalypse.”

Heart Machine is the latest studio to hemorrhage employees after Double Fine laid off around 25% of its staff in late July. These layoffs were a direct result of the studio going independent due to Xbox’s massive restructuring efforts this summer, which saw the two companies part ways, though Double Fine got to keep its IPs in the amicable ‘divorce.’

Despite this setback, Double Fine founder Tim Schafer has made it clear that he’s moving forward at full speed, saying “no one puts Double Fine out of business besides me” — and fans are hopeful that Heart Machine will also survive this latest hit with a similar amount of moxie.

And earlier today, multiple employees at Build a Rocket Boy announced that they were laid off , casting further doubt onto the studio's future following Mindseye's rocky launch last year.

articles.title: RAVEN2 - ZERO Lets Players Enter an Apocalyptic MMORPG Where Growth Is Tied to Gameplay
articles.body:
Netmarble's Raven2 is a blockbuster dark fantasy MMORPG with a player base that covers the globe. Fans from 155 countries can't get enough of creating their own custom avatar down to the last detail before guiding them through a strife-filled world where you're often forced to fight for your very existence.

With so much fighting in Raven2, it's easy to feel "shut out" of the adventure before you even have a chance to get your bearings. The Raven2 – Zero server update lets you get a fresh start with less pressure to spend money. Thanks to its redesigned progression system and overhauled competitive structure, less-entrenched Raven2 players can quickly get a foothold in the game just by playing it and earning valuable rewards. That means the Zero update lets you remain competitive in its apocalyptic world without fear of getting merc'd because you didn't pay up to get an edge over everyone else.

Raven2 – Zero lets you choose from 10 different classes, with each one offering a new combat style. Marked with the dreaded Cursed Stigma, your role is to vanquish demons and monsters as you travel across the world to investigate strange happenings in a dying land.

A dying land that's also highly competitive. Raven2 – Zero is the ideal option for anyone who feels like they've been pushed out of Raven2's because of hardcore PvP competition between established players. Raven2 – Zero is a much-more laid back server that's focused on lowering the adventure's barrier to early progression. It does this by greatly reducing quest requirements and increasing EXP gained from fighting monsters. Accuracy balance has also been re-adjusted so that players can progress through hunting areas with more ease.

Raven2 – Zero also reduces pressure to spend money on progression by excluding Mythic-grade Holy Garments, Familiars, and Awakenings on the server. Instead, playing Zero gives you access to a variety of Holy Garments and Familiars. And you can earn Holy Garments and Familiars - the highest-graded equipment available on Zero by participating in events. Everyone must build themselves up by progressing through the game, not by immediately buying top gear.

And there's lots to discover when other players aren't out for your blood. You're left free to enjoy the fundamental Raven2 – Zero MMORPG farming experience, especially since Zero bumps up equipment drop rates for field loot drops. A pretty fitting reward for sticking it out on fields filled with abominations.

Field hunting is also how you collect "Farming Crystals," a new currency that you can only collect while playing the game. These crystals can be exchanged for key items from the Shop, so your hard work is directly rewarded. And new accuracy balances means your contributions in large-scale battles are registered instead of being chalked up to miss after miss.

The Raven2 - Zero update welcomes new players. Everyone who joins is gifted the [Zero] Special Starter Package, which contains the Heroic-grade Holy Garments and Familiars. You can also look forward to receiving 550 Summon scrolls, as well as Legendary Holy Garments and Familiars, all of which will go a long way to growing your character without tons of grinding. More Heroic-grade equipment and level milestone rewards are coming through other events to further reduce spending pressure , Lapsed players are especially welcome to join the server via some Welcome Back events that offer Legendary Holy Garment and Familiar, 330 Summons and more, alongside an ongoing Burning Event designed to support faster progression - making this an ideal time to jump into or return to Raven2.

Entering a new MMORPG that's been around for a while is kind of like entering a new school where everyone's friend groups are already established. Raven2 – Zero eliminates that sinking feeling by giving everyone the same level ground to stand on. There's still tons of fighting to be done on this new server, but it's more about wailing on monsters than fighting other players. You're free to carve your own life in Raven 2 – Zero, even if the life of someone marked by the Cursed Stigma is usually brutal.

articles.title: The WD Green SN3000 1TB PCIe 4.0 M.2 NVME Solid State Drive (SSD) Drops to $129 at Newegg
articles.summary: PS5 compatible with caveats.
articles.body:
Newegg is offering one of the lowest prices I've seen this year for a brand name M.2 SSD. Newegg via its official AliExpress storefront is offering a WD Green SN3000 1TB PCIe 4.0 M.2 NVMe Solid State Drive for an impressively low price of $129.48 with free shipping after you apply $15 off coupon code " 15USAFF ". This same drive sells for $160 on Amazon .

1TB WD Green SN3000 M.2 PCIe 4x4 SSD for $129.48

WD Green SN3000 1TB PCIe Gen4 x4 M.2 SSD (up to 5,000MBps)

The WD Green SN3000 is fast for a "budget" M.2 SSD. This is a DRAM-less PCI-E 4x4 drive equipped with SanDisk's QLC 3D NAND memory and boasting transfer speeds of up to 5,000MB/s read and 4,200MB/s write. This is an ideal boot drive for your gaming PC, but it's also fully compatible with the PlayStation 5 console. It's a bit under Sony's recommended minimum requirement of 5,5000MB/s, but you likely won't notice the speed difference except maybe during game installations when you are moving large files.

Installing an SSD in your PlayStation 5 console is super easy and won't void your warranty. It's also a near essential upgrade. With games taking up as much as 100GB apiece, it's very easy to max out the PS5's stock 1TB storage (which is actually just 667MB of usable storage ). In fact, it's not unheard of for an avid PS5 gamer to cap out even with 2TB.

Although you can get by without a heatsink, Sony officially recommends one, as noted in their FAQ section in their install guide. The WD Green SN3000 doesn't include one out of the box. Fortunately, you can find one on Amazon for about $6 and they're very simple to install (most are attached with adhesive).

articles.title: GTA 5 Franklin Voice Actor Clears the Air After Calling Out Twitch Star Kai Cenat for Allegedly Breaking Promise to a Young Fan
articles.summary: The voice actor behind GTA 5’s Franklin went viral after revealing his personal disagreement with famous Twitch steamer Kai Cenat, but the two stars are on good terms again.
articles.body:
The voice actor behind GTA 5’s Franklin went viral after revealing his personal disagreement with famous Twitch steamer Kai Cenat, but the two stars are on good terms again.

Shawn ‘Solo’ Fonteno is the voice behind one of Grand Theft Auto ’s most iconic characters, Franklin Clinton. He made an appearance on Kai Cenat’s Twitch stream as a special guest back in 2024, where he took the influencer on a tour of the neighborhoods in Los Angeles that appeared in the game’s fictional city of Los Santos.

However, Solo said this was likely the last stream he’d ever do with Cenat due to the broadcaster’s interaction with a young fan that happened during their outing.

Even More GTA 6 Screenshots from Rockstar Games

In a September 2026 episode of the Dope As Usual podcast, Solo explained that Kai Cenat approached a young fan during the stream who came from a struggling family. According to Solo, Cenat had offered to buy the fan a motorcycle — but Solo says he never made good on that promise.

“This was a family that didn’t have much at all, bro,” he recalled. “It was probably 15 people living in a one-bedroom home. I know these people, and I help them out at times. …Kai was cool, cordial with them, talking to them, ‘What you want? What can I get you?’ And the kid was like, ‘I wanna bike, can you get me a bike?’ He said, ‘What kind of bike?’ and the kid said, ‘A motorcycle!’ He said, ‘We gon’ make it happen.’

“I persisted to keep calling after that… let about a week go by, and texted, texted, tried to call, ‘Hey man, honor that [promise] with this kid, bro. It’s just a bike. [It’d] probably be about a thousand dollars, twelve hundred dollars or less, I don’t know, but you gave that kid this promise. And now you’re making me look bad, because I brought you here, and you gave this kid that promise.’”

Solo said he even approached Kai’s friend and fellow streamer Fanum about the issue, who the actor says ignored him.

“I’m standing on it, man,” he continued. “I’ll look into any one of these cameras like, ‘Bro, you a f**ked up dude for that.’ To me. You’re a very f**ked up dude. I don’t give a f**k how you feel about it. To me, that was not cool. If I make a promise, especially to a kid, I’mma honor it.”

The podcast went viral, prompting a wave of backlash toward Kai Cenat for allegedly failing to keep his promise to the child. Fans were convinced that he and Solo now had bad blood as a result of this issue — but just a day later, Solo confirmed that he and Kai were on good terms once more.

Solo revealed the news in an Instagram comment on September 16, which he wrote in response to a clip from the podcast episode. “I just talked to Kai and it was an honest mistake and it’s fixed. Thanks @kaicenat,” he said.

GTA fervor is at an all-time high after Rockstar’s immensely-popular preview for Grand Theft Auto 6 aired on Netflix last month. Fans can’t wait for the highly-anticipated game to finally release in November, and with major music artists and platforms like Spotify dropping cheeky hints on social media and billboards across Los Angeles, it’s clear there’s a lot more in store as the clock ticks down to launch in two months.

articles.title: Spotify Seems to Be Teasing a GTA 6 Collaboration with Rockstar Games
articles.summary: Spotify appears to be the next big streaming giant to partner with Rockstar Games for GTA 6's marketing.
articles.body:
Spotify appears to be the next big streaming giant to partner with Rockstar Games for GTA 6's marketing.

The music streaming service has begun putting up billboards in Los Angeles and New York featuring the GTA 6 artwork that was released by various artists yesterday . Travis Scott, Future, Morgan Wallen, and a handful of other musicians all posted unique artwork that resembled Rockstar's signature style, but neglected to reveal exactly what they were teasing. This cryptic tease now appears to involve Spotify.

Many assumed that this was Rockstar's way of teasing these artists might have music in the game, but it may be much bigger than that. Some running theories have speculated that the artists could release exclusive music for GTA 6, something Rockstar did with Dr. Dre for a GTA Online update a few years ago. However, Spotify's inclusion may mean there's even more to this; the platform might provide exclusive teases of some music that could be featured in GTA 6 ahead of the game's release as part of its marketing push.

More billboards from Spotify IG pic.twitter.com/CLX6lK3MIW — Tex2 (@TexFunz2) September 16, 2026

More billboards from Spotify IG pic.twitter.com/CLX6lK3MIW

Some have also theorized that GTA 6 may have some kind of Spotify integration, allowing users to listen to their own Spotify playlists in-game. Given how much money Rockstar spends on curating music for its games and how much effort goes into crafting its radio stations, it seems difficult to imagine this, but it's entirely possible. Either way, it's clear Spotify has some kind of partnership with Rockstar Games on GTA 6.

Rockstar previously teamed up with Netflix to debut the first gameplay trailer for GTA 6, resulting in the premiere being the most-watched thing on the streamer during its first week. Rockstar Games personally pitched the idea to Netflix , so it wouldn't be surprising if a similar thing is happening with Spotify. Rockstar is also planning to do all kinds of unprecedented marketing in Miami , with signage being built as we speak in the city.

GTA 6 will officially be two months away from release this Saturday, so it wouldn't be surprising if Rockstar plans to put an end to all the teasing and unveil what it's doing with Spotify by the end of the week.
